title: The light above (7.10)
hook: he enters within and sees a light above his mind
tomorrow: if everything God made is good, where does the rot come from?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a man let go of picturing God as a body the size of space. Your line: beyond the picture.

When a boss says a decision is above your pay grade, nobody looks at the ceiling. Above can mean something besides higher up. Augustine needs that other meaning. Once God isn't a body up in the sky, where does he look? Inside. The books, he says, warned him to return to himself, so he went into his own depths, with God as his guide. And there, above his own mind, he saw a light. Then comes an odd line: it wasn't above him the way oil floats above water. So what kind of above is it?
screen: `ABOVE YOUR PAY GRADE.` → `HE LOOKS INSIDE.` → `NOT LIKE OIL ON WATER.`

segments.voice: First, the way in. Not the stars this time. His own mind, with the eye of his soul, as he puts it. Second, what the light was not. Not the ordinary light anyone can see. Not a bigger, brighter version of it, filling everything. Other, he says, far other. Third, the puzzle solved. It wasn't above his mind the way oil sits on water, or the sky stretches over the earth. It was above him because it made him, and he was below it because he was made by it. Above means maker, not altitude. A little like an author and a story: the author isn't on a higher shelf, but the story comes from her. Fourth, a name. He says he heard, as if from far off, the name God gives Moses at the burning bush, in the Douay-Rheims: "I AM WHO AM." He heard it the way the heart hears, and he could sooner doubt he was alive than doubt that truth is. And he says he trembled, with love and with awe. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: Augustine's Latin for what he saw is lucem incommutabilem, the light that doesn't change. Notice the order. Within first: he had to come home to himself. Then above: the light was not himself.
screen: `FIRST, INWARD.` · `NOT ORDINARY LIGHT.` · `ABOVE, BECAUSE IT MADE HIM.` · `I AM WHO AM.` · then, large: `WITHIN, THEN ABOVE.`

segments.voice: Sit tall and let your eyes rest on your hands in your lap: notice your breath, your body, the thoughts passing through. Then, slowly, lift your gaze to the highest point in the room, not to find God up there, but as your body's way of saying above. If you pray, you can rest in the name he heard: I AM WHO AM.
The light above. What Augustine saw within: not over his mind like oil on water, but above it as its maker.
Within, then above: going inward is the road, not the end of it. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: tried looking inward on my run. found zero light. just noise about the coach. so does it actually work?
options: Inward is step one. Augustine's light wasn't his own noise; it was above his mind, the one who made it.
Then the noise is the answer. Augustine says the light inside was just his own mind, cleared up.
Try looking up instead. Augustine found the light by watching the sky, not by looking inside.
chat.meaning: Augustine went within, then above: the light wasn't his own mind but what made it. Inward is the road, not the destination.

notes: Douay-Rheims Exodus 3:14: 'God said to Moses: I AM WHO AM.' Only 'I AM WHO AM' is quoted. Confirm.

Confessions 7.10 paraphrased: admonished to return to himself, he entered his inward self with God as guide; saw with the eye of his soul, above his mind, the Light Unchangeable; not this common light nor a greater of the same kind, but other, far other; not above as oil above water or heaven above earth, but above because it made him; he trembled with love and awe; he heard from afar 'I am that I am', as the heart hears, and could sooner doubt he lived than that Truth is. Confirm.
Latin 'lucem incommutabilem' (7.10.16, accusative) quoted; the original game gives the nominative 'lux incommutabilis'. Confirm forms and pronunciations.
